parsed.explanation: Thin, partly undated dossier, so I extrapolate from structural signals. Two sources report state police in the national-authority areas arresting and torturing gay residents, with two explicit homosexuality prosecutions in an unfixed three-year window. A queer organisation was banned by police, followed by hate messages. Same-sex criminalisation is contested: the 1936 ordinance (up to 10 years) is held in force by some monitors and not by others. There is no legal gender recognition, no statutory non-discrimination route, and no trans-specific violence count. Social acceptance ranks 130th (2010-2020 window). Family and social persecution is reported, and about 90 LGBT residents fled. Border, document, facility and detention rules are unsourced, so they remain open questions rather than established exposures. The 1960-code region is decriminalised, but the regime is patchy and the recourse gap is real. Overall this sits in the high-risk band, not severe, because no trans-specific organised targeting or execution is documented.
